common_name: Spanish Flare Hellebore (Honeymoon Series Lenten Rose)

planting.note: Plant container-grown divisions in fall or early spring into humus-rich, well-drained shade soil; established clumps resent being moved.

directions: Part of the Honeymoon series bred by Hans Hansen, this hellebore carries light yellow outward-facing flowers about 3 inches across, each marked with a central maroon flare at the base of the petals. Flowers open in late winter into early-to-mid spring above a mound of leathery, evergreen foliage. Like other Lenten roses it is largely pest-resistant and tolerates competition from tree roots once established. Mulch lightly in fall to protect emerging buds from hard freezes.

common_name: Rio Carnival Hellebore (Honeymoon Series Lenten Rose)

planting.note: Set out divisions in fall or early spring in part shade with rich, well-drained soil; avoid disturbing roots once the clump is settled.

directions: This Honeymoon-series selection, also from Hans Hansen's breeding program, produces single 2.5-3 inch blooms in light yellow heavily speckled with burgundy red, giving each flower a freckled, carnival-like look. It flowers from late winter through mid-spring over clumps of semi-evergreen, deeply lobed foliage. Clumps slowly bulk up over several seasons and can eventually be divided to make new plants. It is deer- and rabbit-resistant, a useful trait for shaded beds under browsing pressure.

common_name: French Kiss Hellebore (Honeymoon Series Lenten Rose)

planting.note: Install divisions in fall or early spring into shaded beds amended with compost; established plants are long-lived and best left undisturbed.

directions: French Kiss bears large single flowers, 3 to 3.5 inches across, in white with fine raspberry-pink veining radiating from the center, nodding over a mound of leathery evergreen leaves. Bloom runs from late winter into mid-spring, making it a reliable early-season nectar source for emerging pollinators. As with other Honeymoon series plants from this breeding line, it tends toward vigorous, uniform clumps compared to older open-pollinated hybridus seed strains. It appreciates consistent moisture while establishing but tolerates drier shade once rooted in.

common_name: Whirlwind Romance Hellebore (Wedding Party Series Lenten Rose)

planting.note: Plant divisions in fall or early spring in part shade to shade with fertile, well-drained soil; clumps dislike frequent transplanting.

directions: Whirlwind Romance is a Wedding Party series hellebore with white petals overlaid in dark burgundy veining, the reverse of each petal washed in the same deep burgundy so the nodding flowers read dark from outside and pale from within. It flowers from late winter into mid-spring above a low, spreading rosette of evergreen foliage. Like its series-mates it forms a tidy, well-branched clump useful for mass planting under deciduous trees and shrubs. Removing tattered old foliage in late winter helps display the emerging flower stems.

common_name: True Love Hellebore (Wedding Party Series Lenten Rose)

planting.note: Set divisions out in fall or early spring in shaded, humus-rich soil; avoid wet, poorly drained sites that can rot the crown.

directions: True Love produces fully double flowers, 3 to 3.5 inches across, in a rich maroon-red that holds its color well as the blooms age. Flowering begins in late winter and continues into mid-spring over a compact mound of dark, leathery evergreen leaves. The double form gives a fuller, rose-like appearance compared to single-flowered hybridus types, and the flowers hold up well as cut stems floated in shallow water. It is unappealing to deer and rabbits, making it a dependable choice for unfenced shade gardens.

common_name: Maid of Honor Hellebore (Wedding Party Series Lenten Rose)

planting.note: Install in fall or early spring in part shade to shade with well-drained, organically rich soil; established clumps need little maintenance.

directions: Maid of Honor carries double flowers, roughly 2 to 3 inches across, in shades ranging from light to dark pink on the same plant as blooms mature. Bloom extends from late winter into mid-spring above evergreen, deeply divided foliage that stays attractive through the growing season. The layered petal form gives individual flowers a fuller, peony-like look than single-flowered Lenten rose types. Light winter mulch helps protect the earliest flower buds from hard freezes in colder parts of its range.

common_name: Wedding Bells Hellebore (Wedding Party Series Lenten Rose)

planting.note: Plant divisions in fall or early spring into shaded beds with fertile, well-drained soil; let clumps establish undisturbed for best bloom.

directions: Wedding Bells produces clear white double flowers, about 2 to 2.5 inches across, that nod cleanly above a low mound of evergreen, finely divided leaves. It flowers from late winter into mid-spring, brightening shaded borders before most other perennials emerge. Pure white blooms show especially well against dark foliage or evergreen groundcovers, and flowers often pick up a faint green blush as they age. Because it holds its foliage year-round, cut back only tattered or winter-damaged leaves in late winter rather than shearing the whole plant.

common_name: Flower Girl Hellebore (Wedding Party Series Lenten Rose)

planting.note: Set out divisions in fall or early spring in part shade to shade with humus-rich, well-drained soil; avoid moving established clumps.

directions: Flower Girl bears double flowers, around 2.5 to 3 inches across, in soft blush to light pink tones that soften as the bloom ages. Flowering runs from late winter into mid-spring over an evergreen rosette of leathery, palmately divided leaves. The gentle pink coloring pairs well with white-flowered series-mates such as Wedding Bells in mixed shade plantings. Like other Wedding Party hellebores it is slow to spread but long-lived, rewarding patient gardeners with larger flower counts each season.
